implements_gap: K13 tool/channel audit group 3 decision D2: tool-calling code sandbox (execute_code / code_kernel / code_execution_env / code_execution_rpc). This batch records the reference facts, the V2 mapping and four options (S1 no port, S2 restricted compute sandbox, S3 full programmatic tool calling, S4 remote/container as a separate contract), the honest non-security-boundary statement, the no-write/no-terminal RPC rule, the worker-protocol coordination ask and the test plan. NOT implementation: no source/test/migration/route/worker change

facts: execute_code is programmatic tool calling: the model writes Python that calls tools over RPC, only stdout returns; local backend is a persistent per-conversation kernel (UDS, loopback TCP on Windows)
SANDBOX_ALLOWED_TOOLS = web_search/web_extract/read_file/write_file/search_files/patch/terminal intersected with the session toolsets (write tools and terminal included)
limits: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=300s, DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS=50, stdout 50KB head/tail 40/60 plus a spill file <=5MB, stderr 10KB

code_kernel: one child per (owner, mode, interpreter, cwd, tool-set); state survives; same security envelope as per-call (env scrub, RPC token + per-cell tool budget, ANSI strip + secret redaction); a wedged kernel is killed; env frozen at spawn until reset=true; JSON line protocol with a per-kernel SENTINEL; max_session_kernels LRU; delegated child kernels keyed parent::child and disposed on cleanup
code_execution_env does child env scrubbing and interpreter/cwd resolution; code_execution_rpc provides UDS/loopback RPC servers with token auth and call budgets
browser_exec requires the terminal surface because it runs arbitrary host Python (same execution-surface family)
reference.adaptation: V2 has only shell_execute (one-shot approved argv) and files_*; no host Python, no persistent kernel, no tool RPC. The contract maps the reference to four V2 options and explicitly states that a process-level subprocess is NOT a security boundary; the sandbox must not bridge terminal or write tools without a separate approval design, and S3 would change the shared worker protocol (A coordination)

decision_questions: S1 no port (recommended first, record non-parity) / S2 restricted compute sandbox (recommended second: no RPC bridge, temp cwd, env scrub, resource bounds, non-security-boundary statement) / S3 full PTC (read-only RPC allowlist + persistent kernel, A protocol coordination) / S4 remote/container separate contract
S2 details: fixed interpreter, wall clock/stdout bounds, read workspace via stdin only, import policy, default OFF + owner enable
S3 details: read-only RPC allowlist, kernel lifecycle/LRU/reclaim, cancellation/resource-lock interaction, delegated child kernel ownership, audit events
security: no write/terminal tools over RPC; never claim real isolation; no credential inheritance
